Fact.Name: A signer of this return is barred from the Self-Select PIN method
Fact.Description:
True when a signer of this return is a first-time filer who was younger than 16 at the end of the tax year — the population the Form 1040 instructions bar from the Self-Select PIN method. True for the primary filer who is under 16 and did not file last year, and, on a return treated as MFJ, for a spouse under 16 who did not file last year.
THIS IS THE BODY OF THE RETIRED KNOCKOUT /flowKnockoutFirstTimeFilerYoungerThan16, UNCHANGED, under a name that says what the printed rule says. The rule bars ONE SIGNATURE METHOD, not filing: the same instructions page leaves the Practitioner PIN and the handwritten paper signature open to exactly this filer. So this fact is an INPUT to /signatureMethodRoute and carries neither BlockSubmissionOnTrue nor membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.
COMPLETENESS IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Both arms read Any(Not(IsComplete(<answer>)), Not(<answer>)) — not-yet-answered counts as not-yet-filed — so this fact is Complete in every state of the signing answers and Incomplete only where the DATE OF BIRTH itself is unanswered. That property was bought by a measured leak in the predecessor's fix round 1 and it is what keeps /signatureMethodRoute TOTAL wherever the age is known. Under a routing fact the unanswered state now costs nothing: it OFFERS the paper path rather than refusing the return, and over-offering paper is free.
THE /filedLastYear PROXY IS DISSOLVED RATHER THAN FIXED. It answers "did you file LAST year" where the printed rule says "first-time filer", so a filer who last filed two years ago is over-caught. Under a refusal that was an over-refusal; under a route its only consequence is which method is offered. A separate "have you ever filed" intake would sharpen the offer and is not a prerequisite of anything.

Fact.Name: Signature method options
Fact.Description:
The three signature methods the 2025 Instructions for Form 1040 leave open to an individual return: the Self-Select PIN, the Practitioner PIN, and a handwritten signature on a paper return. A CLOSED set — the instructions name no fourth.
EXPORTED rather than left to the optionsPath reference alone: /signatureMethodRoute names this set inside a Switch's Then arms, and an optionsPath reference in that position is NOT a dependency edge in the engine-emitted manifest (measured — lint_wiring reported the fact UNWIRED with the route already shipping). The Export is also the honest reading: the option set is what a caller renders the choice from.

Fact.Name: The return is signed through a tax practitioner using the Practitioner PIN method
Fact.Description:
Whether this return is being filed electronically through a tax practitioner who will enter or generate the filer's PIN.
THIS IS THE ARM THE DICTIONARY HAD NO FACT FOR, and it is why a routing fact needed an intake rather than only a derivation. The Self-Select PIN machinery ships in full (/signReturnIdentity and its option set, /selfSelectPin, the spouse twins) and the paper path ships as /isPaperPath; the Practitioner PIN was named nowhere. A route with two arms would have left a first-time under-16 filer with paper as their only alternative, which is a worse answer than the instructions give them.
Optional and complete-safe by its reader: /signatureMethodRoute tests All(IsComplete(this), this), so an unanswered question routes as "not a practitioner return" rather than making the route Incomplete. Whether and how the question is ASKED is the application's surface, not this dictionary's, under invariant #7 — the same division of labor scheduleH:/householdEmployees draws.

Fact.Name: Which signature method this return uses — Self-Select PIN, Practitioner PIN, or paper
Fact.Description:
The signature method this return is on. A ROUTE, not a gate: it changes which method is offered, never whether the return may be filed, and nothing blocks on it.
THE ORDER OF THE ARMS IS THE RULE, and each one is printed. (1) paper when /isPaperPathDueToMissingIpPin. FIRST, ahead of the practitioner arm, because the missing-IP-PIN bar is a bar on ANY ELECTRONIC RETURN rather than on one method: "all six digits of your IP PIN must appear" ... "in the IP PIN spaces provided next to the" "space for your occupation for your elec-" "tronic signature to be complete. Failure" "to include an issued IP PIN on the elec-" "tronic return will result in an invalid sig-" "nature and a rejected return." A filer with an issued IP PIN they cannot supply cannot e-file THROUGH A PRACTITIONER either, so paper is their route and the practitioner answer must not override it. (2) practitionerPin when the filer says a tax practitioner will enter or generate their PIN. Ahead of the under-16 bar, because that bar is on the SELF-SELECT PIN alone: the instructions offer the Practitioner PIN to exactly the filer the CAUTION box excludes, so a practitioner return is not routed to paper on account of age. (3) paper when /barredFromSelfSelectPin — the first-time under-16 signer the CAUTION box names. This is the population that used to be REFUSED. (4) paper when /isPaperPath's REMAINING legs: a filer (or spouse) who answered cannotFind to the Self-Select PIN identity question. That fact's own option set already calls cannotFind "this dictionary's own escape to the paper path", so the route reads it rather than inventing a second one. Note the whole of /isPaperPath is tested here, missing-IP-PIN leg included; arm (1) has already caught that leg, so this arm decides only the cannotFind ones. (5) selfSelectPin otherwise.
TOTAL WHEREVER THE AGE IS KNOWN, which is obligation (3) of the contract this discharges. Arm (1) and arm (3) are wrapped All(IsComplete(x), x), so an unanswered practitioner question or an unanswered signing identity question resolves the arm Complete-false instead of leaving the route Incomplete; arm (2) is Complete in every state of the signing answers by /barredFromSelfSelectPin's own construction. The route is therefore Incomplete only where a signer's DATE OF BIRTH is unanswered — the one state the retired guard was Incomplete in too, and no return reaches submission without a date of birth.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM. It takes no position on the SCREENS: the application owns those, and invariant #7 excludes the frontend as a ground for REFUSING, not the division of labour. It also claims no MeF element — this repo holds no schema for a signature-method code, and the route is exported for downstream readers only.
WHAT IT REPLACES: /flowKnockoutFirstTimeFilerYoungerThan16, which blocked submission for this filer. Under a route the filer has somewhere to go, so there is nothing left to refuse.
